rounds.text: Aditya Infotech Ltd is demonstrating exceptional operational momentum, evidenced by a 65% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a 212% surge in profit growth [E16, E19]. The company has successfully scaled its market share from 30% at the time of its IPO to 42% as of September 2026, with management now projecting a further increase to 45% by FY2027 [E72, E84]. This growth is supported by a robust expansion of manufacturing capabilities, including a new lens plant and the upcoming launch of a cable facility, while the company has simultaneously achieved a debt-free status as of October 2026 [E78, E80, E88]. Institutional confidence is clearly rising, as evidenced by a positive money flow and increased holdings from both foreign and domestic institutions [E36, E37, E38]. Conceded: the stock trades at a high P/E of 80.9x and a P/B of 13.63x, and the recent cash conversion ratio of 0.04x indicates that reported profits are currently significantly outpacing operating cash flow [E1, E2, E28]. Despite these valuation concerns, the company’s ability to maintain high returns on equity and capital, alongside aggressive revenue guidance of 54–61% growth for FY2027, suggests that the business is rapidly growing into its premium valuation [E12, E13, E74].

Aditya Infotech trades at extreme valuation multiples, including a P/E ratio of 80.9x [E1] compared to the sector benchmark of 21.21x [E6], a P/B ratio of 13.63x versus the sector average of 2.31x [E2, E7], and an EV/EBITDA of 54.5x against a sector benchmark of 12.22x [E11]. This excessive pricing leaves a DCF margin of safety of -106.9% based on an intrinsic value of Rs 1,969 per share [E39, E40], with the market price requiring 28.2% earnings growth against the 18.0% base case assumption [E41]. Underlying cash generation severely lags reported profits, evidenced by a cash conversion ratio of just 0.04x for March 2026 [E28], negative free cash flow of Rs -120 Cr [E30], and working capital days inflating from 40.8 to 73.9 days [E58]. Operational and margin pressures are intensifying as phenomenal cost hikes in critical components like SOC, DDR, and flash memory forced the company to absorb input costs in Q2 [E75, E81, E92], while a fire at the Kadapa plant caused a one-time loss of Rs 34.4 Cr [E90]. Adding to governance caution, promoter ownership has dropped by 5.32 percentage points year-on-year to 71.80% [E35, E57]. Conceded: the company exhibits strong trailing operational performance, highlighted by TTM sales growth of 65% [E16], TTM profit growth of 212% [E19], and an ROCE of 28.6% [E12]. Nevertheless, given that annualised price volatility stands at 54.3% [E48], the market is heavily overpaying for growth that is not currently converting into positive free cash flow [E30, E66].

Conceded: the company trades at a rich P/E of 80.9x and a P/B of 13.63x [E1, E2, E6, E7], and the DCF model estimates intrinsic value at Rs 1,969 against a higher market price [E39, E40]. However, labeling these multiples as excessive ignores the company's compounding engine, including 65% TTM sales growth [E16], a 212% surge in TTM profit growth [E19], and an exceptional 28.6% ROCE [E12] that completely eclipses the sector median of 13.5% [E71]. The reported cash conversion of 0.04x and negative free cash flow of Rs -120 Cr in March 2026 [E28, E30] are decisively neutralized by subsequent balance sheet transformations: the company raised Rs 1,500 crores via a QIP in September and completely repaid all borrowings by October, leaving the business entirely debt-free with substantial cash reserves [E87, E88, E89]. While the bear highlights input cost pressures in SOC and DDR and a Rs 34.4 Cr fire loss at Kadapa [E75, E81, E90, E92], management confirmed that this fire loss is fully covered by insurance with claims already lodged [E91], and strong pricing power is reflected in upwardly revised FY27 revenue guidance of up to Rs 6,800 crores [E73] alongside a rapidly expanding market share target of 43% to 45% [E72]. Finally, the reduction in promoter holding [E35, E57] is heavily outweighed by aggressive institutional accumulation, with foreign and domestic institutional holdings expanding significantly and driving positive institutional money flow [E36, E37, E38].

The bull’s reliance on recent growth metrics ignores that the market has already priced in an aggressive 28.2% earnings growth rate, which exceeds the base case assumption of 18.0% [E41]. While the bull points to a 212% profit surge [E19], this is heavily contrasted by the fact that cash conversion remains alarmingly low at 0.04x, indicating that reported profits are not translating into actual cash flow [E28]. Conceded: the company has successfully raised capital and repaid debt [E87, E88]. However, this does not mitigate the fundamental valuation risk where the stock trades at a P/E of 84.25x compared to a sector benchmark of 21.21x [E6], and a P/B of 13.61x against a sector benchmark of 2.31x [E7]. Furthermore, the bull overlooks that working capital days have significantly increased from 40.8 to 73.9 days [E58], signaling potential inefficiencies in operations that could pressure future margins. Finally, the reliance on insurance to cover the Kadapa plant fire [E91] and the admission that the company is absorbing phenomenal cost hikes in critical components like SOC and DDR [E92] suggest that the company’s profitability is vulnerable to external shocks that management cannot fully control.

The bear’s concern regarding the reverse DCF [E41] ignores that the company has consistently outperformed expectations, with profit growth of 212% [E19] and sales growth of 65% [E16] significantly outpacing historical benchmarks. While the bear highlights low cash conversion [E28], this is a snapshot of a single period that ignores the company’s massive recent capital raise of INR 1,500 crores [E87] and its transition to a debt-free status [E88], which fundamentally strengthens the balance sheet. Conceded: working capital days have increased [E58] and the P/E ratio is higher than the sector benchmark [E6]. However, these metrics fail to account for the company’s aggressive expansion, including new capacity coming online [E34] and the strategic rollout of high-margin enterprise products [E93, E95]. The bear’s focus on the Kadapa fire [E90] overlooks that the loss is fully covered by insurance [E91], and the company’s ability to raise revenue guidance to 54–61% growth [E73, E74] demonstrates that management is successfully navigating input cost pressures [E92]. Finally, the shift in institutional holdings toward a positive money flow [E38] confirms that sophisticated investors are prioritizing the company’s 42% market share [E84] and its dominant competitive position over short-term valuation multiples.

Conceded: the company successfully raised INR 1,500 crores in its QIP [E87] and is now debt-free [E88]. However, the bull's dismissal of the poor cash conversion [E28] and rising working capital days—from 40.8 to 73.9 days [E58]—ignores that March 2026 free cash flow plunged to negative Rs 120 Cr [E30] despite reported profits. While the bull waves away the Kadapa plant fire incident [E90], the occurrence of operational disruptions alongside an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend [E26, E27] underscores execution risk that a 54% to 61% revenue guidance hike [E73, E74] cannot simply erase. Furthermore, pointing to strong historical profit growth [E19] and institutional money flow [E38] does not justify a P/E of 80.9x [E1] and EV/EBITDA of 54.5x [E11] sitting at massive premiums over sector benchmarks [E6, E11]. Finally, the bull's optimism on enterprise products [E93, E95] ignores that management is already forced to absorb phenomenal input cost hikes in SOC and memory components [E92], which caused gross margins to contract slightly below Q1 levels down to 30.0% in Q2 [E81, E82].
